title: Beatrix and the Oath
premise: Ansel Delacroix, the last of the oath-bound swordspeakers, has spent a decade hiding in the Thornfell mountains, trading on smugglers' roads and burying the magic that once bound his order to the crown. When Beatrix, a mute child who speaks only in the dead tongue of the First Kings, collapses at his door pursued by crown wardens, Ansel learns she carries the true name of the king—proof that the thing wearing his sovereign's face is a hollow-wraith that devours oaths and memories alike. Guided by Beatrix's fragments and the reluctant loyalty of his found family of smugglers, Ansel descends into the capital at midwinter, where he must speak the unbinding oath aloud—a spell that will erase every memory he has of those he loves. He speaks it anyway; the king is freed, the wraith unmade, and though Ansel forgets Beatrix entirely, she stays by his side, teaching him her language one word at a time so they can begin again.
about_author: Hazel Vasquez is a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing medieval oath-books before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a farmhouse in the northern hills, where she keeps bees and an ever-growing collection of half-translated dead languages.

chapters.title: The Child Who Spoke Before Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. On a frozen smuggling run, Ansel returns to find a child bleeding on his doorstep, speaking a tongue older than any kingdom—and crown wardens tracking her through the snow. He hides her among his found family of smugglers, but recognizes the words she mouths: they are swordspeech, the oath-language he swore never to use again. Emotional beat: fear giving way to fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: What the Warden Knew
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, rendered through her fragmented understanding. A captured warden reveals the truth: the king died years ago, and the wraith wearing his crown is hunting Beatrix because she alone holds his true name—the one thing that can unmake it. The smugglers vote to shelter her anyway, binding themselves into a family none of them chose but all now defend. Emotional beat: duty transformed into love.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The party fights through the wraith's unnatural winter toward the capital, losing their guide and nearly each other. In a ruined oath-hall, Beatrix teaches Ansel the unbinding rite—and he learns its price: the speaker forgets everyone they love. Torn between duty and devotion, he chooses in silence, telling no one. Emotional beat: quiet heartbreak beneath rising resolve.

chapters.title: Speak, and Begin Again
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climaxing in Ansel's voice. In the throne room, Ansel speaks the unbinding as the wraith unmakes itself screaming; the true name returns to the dying king, who names Beatrix heir before the end. Ansel wakes with no memory of her—but Beatrix remains, patient, beginning to teach him her language word by word. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into hope; love outlasting memory.
